lines.li: [them] It's strange to walk up to your gate as a guest.
[us] It's strange for us to open it to you.
[them] Then we'll both have to get used to it.
[them] Your people haven't taken their eyes off me since I walked in.
[us] Can you blame them?
[them] No, I'd do the same at home.
[them] The green branches we carried to your gate have dried out by now.
[us] And the truce?
[them] That's still green, as far as my people are concerned.
[them] Whoever swore for us did it on the hilt, and we hold to that.
[us] So do we.
[them] Good, a sword sworn on is a hard thing to draw again.
[them] We signed terms with your colony, and terms are terms where I come from.
[us] Here too.
[them] Then we'll get along fine until somebody finds a loophole.
[them] The terms are logged on our side, with your colony's witness marked.
[us] We wrote ours down too.
[them] Then we're both on record, which is the point.
[them] A truce with the Empire is a courtesy we extend, not a right you hold.
[us] Then we'll try to deserve the courtesy.
[them] Your colony asked for the truce, and some at home took it for weakness.
[us] And you?
[them] I took it for sense, and I'm here, aren't I?
[them] We asked for terms after your colony beat us, I won't pretend otherwise.
[us] It takes something to ask.
[them,their:tribal] It took a lot of empty places at the fire.
[them] It took a lot of empty beds at home.
[them] You should know that not everyone at home was glad of the truce.
[us] Should we be worried?
[them,their:rough] With some of my people, it's always worth keeping a watch.
[them] Keep a watch, as you would anyway, and leave it at that.
[them] Some at home want the raids back when the truce ends, and some want peace.
[us] Which do you want?
[them] I'm standing in your yard as a guest, so you can guess.
[them] Between us, I hope this ends as a peace.
[us] So do we.
[them] Then let's both give the hotheads at home nothing to point at.
[us] We'll keep our people's hands still.
[them] And I'll tell them at home how I was treated here.
[us] Not long ago I wouldn't have believed {TRUCEWITH} would come to us as guests.
[them] Not long ago I'd have come with a rifle and a lot of friends.
[us] I'm glad you didn't.
[them] My people remember the day your colony swore an oath with ours.
[us] So do we.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say an oath is a rope between two camps, and pulls both ways.
[them,their:medieval] It was sworn before witnesses, and witnesses have long memories.
[them,their:hightech] It's on record at home, and our records don't get thrown out.
[them] An oath sworn gets talked about for years in my town.
[them] Your colony swore with my people and kept to it, which is rarer than it should be.
[us] We meant it when we swore.
[them] I believe that, and so do most people at home.
[us] Most?
[them] There's always someone who'd rather have had the fight.
[them] I know my people broke a truce with your colony once.
[us] We haven't forgotten it.
[them,their:lowtech] Not all of us swore to it, but all of us carry the shame of it.
[them] Not all of us agreed with the ones who broke it.
[us] That's worth hearing, at least.
[us] Your people broke their truce with us.
[them] And your people never broke a word in their lives, I'm sure.
[them] Your colony broke its truce with my people, and that is still said at home.
[us] It's not something we're proud of.
[them] Good, it shouldn't be.
[them] I don't swear anything with people who break truces.
[us] Then don't, we're only talking.
[them] I heard your colony broke its word to another people.
[us] There's more to it than what you heard.
[them] There always is, and people still repeat the short version.
[them] Word travels with the caravans, and the word on your colony isn't good lately.
[us] What are they saying?
[them] That you broke a truce or a pact, depending on who tells it.
[us] And you came anyway.
[them] I came to trade, not to swear anything.
[them] My people would think twice before swearing anything with your colony.
[us] Because of what you've heard?
[them] Because of what everyone's heard.
